findings.evidence: grep -n 'congrArg (fun f' gives 218, 221, 260, 270, 283, 320, 323, 377, 389; `grep -c 'refine LieEquiv.ext fun x => ?_'` gives 5. `LieEquiv.ext` and `LieEquiv.coe_coe` exist at Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/Basic.lean:574 and :550; `DFunLike.congr_fun` is used in Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/Derivation/Basic.lean:98.
findings.fix: Add one private lemma `serre_equiv_ext {e₁ e₂ : Matrix.ToLieAlgebra R CM ≃ₗ⁅R⁆ L} (hH hE hF) : e₁ = e₂ := LieEquiv.ext fun x => DFunLike.congr_fun (serre_hom_ext (g₁ := e₁.toLieHom) (g₂ := e₂.toLieHom) hH hE hF) x` (`LieEquiv.coe_coe` is `rfl` and `@[simp]`, Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/Basic.lean:550), then each of the five theorems becomes one line `serre_equiv_ext (fun i => by simp) (fun i => by simp) fun i => by simp`. Also replace the explicitly type-ascribed `congrArg (fun f : … => f x)` by `DFunLike.congr_fun … x` throughout.
findings.issue: The same argument — `LieEquiv.ext fun x => ?_`, then a `have h : _.toLieHom = _.toLieHom := serre_hom_ext …`, then `congrArg (fun f : Matrix.ToLieAlgebra R CM →ₗ⁅R⁆ Matrix.ToLieAlgebra R CM => f x) h` — is written out verbatim at lines 255-260, 266-270, 277-283, 370-377 and 385-389, with the same `congrArg` idiom again at 218, 221, 320, 323 (9 hits of `congrArg (fun f`). The reusable fact it hides is that two `LieEquiv`s of the presented algebra agreeing on the generators are equal.

findings.evidence: `Equiv.symm_symm (e) : e.symm.symm = e := rfl` and the `EquivLike` instance setting `inv f := f.invFun` are at Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/Basic.lean:604 and :538; `serreDiagramAut` is defined by the structure literal at Automorphism.lean:213-222 with `invFun := serreDiagramHom R CM (submatrix_perm_symm hσ)`.
findings.fix: For (a), state the composite in both orders as its own private lemma proved directly by `serre_hom_ext` (`serreDiagramHom_symm_comp : (serreDiagramHom R CM hσ).comp (serreDiagramHom R CM (submatrix_perm_symm hσ)) = LieHom.id`) so `right_inv` never needs `σ.symm.symm ≡ σ`. For (b), derive it from `serreChevalleyHom_comp` (or from `serreChevalleyInvolution_symm` plus `LieEquiv.symm_apply_apply`) instead of the `left_inv` field. For (c), keep the one-line proofs but add a short comment noting they hold because `serreDiagramAut`/`serreChevalleyInvolution` are structure literals whose `toLieHom` is the `serreLift`.
findings.issue: Undocumented reliance on definitional equality across wrappers. (a) Line 222 applies `serreDiagramHom_comp R CM (submatrix_perm_symm hσ) hσ`, whose second argument is expected at type `CM.submatrix σ.symm.symm σ.symm.symm = CM`; this only elaborates because `Equiv.symm_symm` is `rfl`, and the resulting `serreDiagramHom` at index `σ.symm.symm` must then be defeq to the one at `σ`. (b) Line 358, `serreChevalleyInvolution_involutive := fun x => (…).left_inv x`, reaches into the raw `left_inv` structure field and needs `invFun` to be defeq to `⇑toLieHom`. (c) The six generator-value lemmas (227, 233, 239, 329, 335, 341) are `serreLift_serreH _ i` etc., which typecheck only by unfolding the structure literal through the `LieEquiv → LieHom → FunLike` coercions. None carries a comment.

summary: The mathematical proofs (`IsSerreSystem.perm`, `.negSwap`, the `submatrix_perm_*` lemmas) are robust and readable, but the equivalence-level results hand-roll the same nine-line extensionality argument nine times instead of factoring it into one lemma, and several steps close only through undocumented definitional equalities across the `LieEquiv`/`LieHom` wrappers.
